raw_response:
I farm 14 mu, not a big place, so I can't gamble too much. For me the safe way is still wheat followed by maize. That rotation is what I know best, and with the well I can protect the crop at the key stages, but water and fertilizer both cost money, so I won't push the rates too high. For wheat, if I want a steady stand and decent ears, I need enough base fertilizer and then one topdress at jointing. I usually watch the leaf color and the soil moisture; if the wheat stays green and we get some rain, I don't add extra beyond the normal plan. After wheat harvest I will plant maize right away, because in Quzhou that window is very tight and losing a few days can cut yield. Maize grows fast in summer, so I mainly spend money on seed, one base fertilizer, one topdress around big flare stage, and one or two irrigations only if rain is short. I would rather keep the plan steady than chase a very high yield and end up with too much cash tied up in inputs.
